newsitem.title: USA: Clinton arrives home for emergency knee surgery.
newsitem.headline: Clinton arrives home for emergency knee surgery.

text.p: President Bill Clinton returned to the Washington area on Friday for emergency surgery to repair a right-knee tendon torn in a late-night stumble during a visit to Florida.

Clinton arrived aboard Air Force One at Andrews Air Force Base in suburban Maryland at about 11:08 a.m. EST (1608 GMT). He was to travel directly to the National Naval Medical Centre in Bethesda, another Maryland suburb, for surgery to repair the tendon.

Clinton stumbled on some "irregular shaped" steps about 1:20 A.M. EST (0620 GMT) on the Florida estate of Australian golfer Greg Norman. Doctors said he tore the quadriceps tendon, which connects the kneecap to the upper thigh in his right leg.

He was due to undergo surgery early in the afternoon at the Bethesda naval hospital, which is the regular provider of medical care for U.S. presidents and has a special wing reserved for that purpose.

Doctors said a local anaesthetic would suffice and the president would remain conscious throughout the surgery. They said his leg would be immobilized in a brace and that he would be on crutches for several weeks.
Clinton nonetheless told reporters as he boarded Air Force One in Florida that he intended to go ahead with his scheduled summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki, Finland, next week.
